title: How to Light a Dark Room Using Sunlight and a Water Bottle
threatLevelText: [ZERO-POWER SOLAR WATER PRISM DAYLIGHTING & 55W INDOOR ROOM ILLUMINATION]
summary: If your home or emergency kit includes rechargeable LED lanterns, solar flashlights, or battery work lights, always use those commercial lighting tools first for the safest and easiest illumination. However, when a major disaster causes a multi-day blackout and daytime [Blast Window Taping](/protocol-31) or blackout boards leave indoor rooms or basements pitch dark, burning candles or a [Tuna Can Oil Wick Heater](/protocol-21) during the day wastes precious night fuel and increases fire and carbon monoxide risks. By filling a salvaged clear 1.5L PET bottle with clean water and 3 drops of unscented household bleach (or half a spoon of coarse salt) to prevent green algae, then sealing it vertically into a hole in a window panel or roof board, water's natural light refraction scatters sunlight 360 degrees—delivering up to 55W bulb brightness indoors for 5+ years with zero electricity.
timeRequired: 30 mins setup and sealing (operates zero-power for 5+ years once installed in daylight)
successRate: 97% (when using a spotless colorless clear bottle, airtight collar sealing, and algae inhibitor)
difficulty: Beginner (No power tools required; uses only a clear bottle, rough stone/sandpaper, water, bleach or salt, and board)
outputPerHour: One 1.5L clear water bottle outputs ~55W incandescent equivalent of cool, fire-free 360-degree indoor daylight

materials.desc: Serves as the optical prism housing that gathers and scatters daylight indoors. Green or brown tinted bottles block light, so choose only crystal-clear unbranded vessels with all labels stripped cleanly.

steps.title: Step 1: Strip All Labels Off a Clear 1.5L Bottle and Lightly Scuff Only the Upper-Third Mounting Band
steps.description:
1. **Pick a Colorless Clear Bottle & Remove Labels**: Peel away every paper label and glue trace, selecting a crystal-clear vessel just like those used in [Solar Water Disinfection (SODIS)](/protocol-23).
2. **Lightly Scuff the Upper-Third Collar Band**: Using sandpaper or a rough stone, lightly frost only the **upper 1/3 waist ring (a two-finger-wide grip band)** where the bottle will lock into the board.
3. **Protect the Lower Two-Thirds Body**: Keep the lower 2/3 cylindrical bulb area completely scratch-free and wiped clean so indoor light radiates brightly.
steps.actionNote: > Why you keep the lower body spotless and scuff only the mounting ring: Sealant and resin slip off glossy smooth surfaces under rain. Scuffing just the 2–3cm collar ring maximizes waterproof grip while keeping optical transmission at 100%.
svgLabels: FIG. 01 // CLEAR 1.5L BOTTLE LABEL STRIP + UPPER 1/3 SCUFF
Peel off all opaque labels and sticky glue residue
Lightly scuff only upper 1/3 band with rough stone
Keep lower 2/3 optical body spotless + scratch-free

deepDive.title: Maximizing Optical Aperture Clarity While Roughening the Collar Bond Surface
deepDive.text: Scratches across the top dome or lower radiating chamber scatter light prematurely inside the bottle wall. Micro-etching solely the **2–3cm mounting collar band** lets pine resin or waterproof sealants anchor mechanically so zero rainwater leaks inside.

steps.title: Step 2: Fill to the Brim with Filtered Water and Add 3 Drops of Bleach (or Salt) to Stop Algae
steps.description:
1. **Fill to the Neck with Clean Water**: Pour clear sediment-free water purified with a [Charcoal-Sand Filter](/protocol-01) or [Cotton Towel Siphon](/protocol-23) all the way up to the bottle neck.
2. **Add 3 Drops of Bleach or Half Spoon Salt**: Drop in **exactly 3 drops of unscented liquid household bleach** (or **half a tablespoon of coarse salt** if bleach is unavailable) so sunlight cannot turn the water cloudy green.
3. **Squeeze Out Air & Seal Tightly**: Gently press to minimize the top air bubble, screw the cap down hard, and seal around the cap rim to stop evaporation.
steps.actionNote: > Why plain water fails within weeks without bleach or salt: Direct sun shining into untreated standing water breeds green algae inside 2–3 weeks, turning your bright skylight into a dim dark-green block. Trace chlorine or salt keeps it crystal-clear for 5+ years.

Add 3 bleach drops or half spoon salt to stop algae

deepDive.title: Omnidirectional Refraction of Water (n=1.33) and Trace Hypochlorite Algae Control
deepDive.text: Water inside a cylinder (refractive index **1.33**) bends vertical sunlight into every direction indoors as a **liquid optical prism**. Trace sodium hypochlorite or high salinity halts photosynthetic algae growth so light brightness stays steady for years.

steps.title: Step 3: Cut a Snug Circular Hole in the Window Blackout Panel and Mount Vertically at a 1:2 Ratio
steps.description:
1. **Cut a Snug Hole Slightly Smaller Than Diameter**: Trace the bottle base on plywood or a [3-Layer Cardboard Thermal Panel](/protocol-22), then trim **half a finger-width (0.5cm) inside the circle** for a tight friction fit.
2. **Add a Notched Collar Flange Ring**: Cut a palm-sized support flange around the seam with radial tabs folded tight around the bottle waist to resist wind.
3. **Mount 1/3 Outside and 2/3 Inside**: Press the bottle vertically so the **upper 1/3 sits outside facing sunlight** and the **lower 2/3 hangs deep inside the dim room**.
steps.actionNote: > Why the 1/3 exterior to 2/3 interior ratio matters: Pushing too little outside starves sunlight capture; pushing too much outside lets light escape outdoors. The 1:2 split maximizes both solar collection above and 360-degree bulb spread below.

Cut hole slightly narrower than body for tight grip
Top 1/3 exposed outside collects wide solar daylight
Bottom 2/3 hanging indoors radiates 360-deg room light

deepDive.text: The outer **1/3 dome** acts as an omnidirectional sky collector while the suspended **2/3 cylinder** scatters refracted rays horizontally and downward via internal wall reflection, brightening even window-blocked disaster rooms evenly.

steps.title: Step 4: Seal the Outer Seam with Resin or Waterproof Backing and Add an Indoor Foil Reflector Skirt
steps.description:
1. **Double-Seal the Exterior Seam**: Coat the scuffed 1/3 ring junction thoroughly with [Pine Resin Waterproof Glue](/protocol-10), oiled clay, or heavy waterproof backing sloped outward so **zero rainwater leaks indoors**.
2. **Attach an Indoor Foil Reflector Ring**: Tape or pin a handspan of shiny kitchen foil around the underside hole edge to bounce stray upward rays back down toward tables and floors, boosting downward brightness 1.5x.
3. **Seat Panel into Window Frame**: Fit the completed panel securely into the window frame with [Blast Window Taping](/protocol-31) for cool, flame-free daytime visibility.
steps.actionNote: > Why meticulous exterior seam sealing is critical: Rainwater creeping along an unsealed collar drips onto indoor bedding and food supplies, risking hypothermia and mold. Always bevel the outer seal downward so rain sheds away.

fatalMistake.title: FATAL // Confusing Bleach/Salt Skylight Water for Drinking Water and Failing to Waterproof the Outer Seam
fatalMistake.description: Water sealed inside a solar bottle contains bleach or heavy salt to suppress algae and must NEVER be drunk; lock and seal the bottle cap permanently with [Pine Resin](/protocol-10) so no one drinks it by mistake during a water crisis. Additionally, poor exterior seam sealing lets rain soak indoor bedding inside your [Cardboard Thermal Capsule](/protocol-22), triggering hypothermia. If contaminated water is accidentally ingested causing vomiting or diarrhea, rehydrate immediately with [Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS)](/protocol-24).
fatalMistake.consequence: Gastric irritation and dehydration from drinking treated skylight water, or rain-soaked shelter hypothermia.

faqs.question: How can apartment dwellers install this without cutting a roof, and how do I block light during blackouts?
faqs.causeDiagnostic: Concrete apartments forbid roof holes, but window frames accept removable blackout panels cleanly.
faqs.resolution: Cut a 3-layer cardboard or plywood panel to fit your window frame, angle the 1.5L bottle hole **30–45 degrees upward toward the sky**, and mount the bottle near the top of the panel to capture indirect sky light horizontally. At night or for blackout privacy, simply slip a dark cloth or [cardboard hood](/protocol-22) over the indoor bottom 2/3.

faqs.question: Does a water bottle skylight still work on cloudy winter days without direct sunbeams?
faqs.causeDiagnostic: Water refraction collects diffuse ambient sky brightness across overcast clouds, not just direct sunbeams.
faqs.resolution: Direct midday sunlight delivers full ~55W bulb output, while overcast or rainy daytime skies still supply **15–25W ambient daylight indoors**—plenty for reading, sorting supplies, and preventing accidents. Placing a crumpled foil reflector tray beneath the outer bottle nose boosts cloudy-day light even further.

shortsScript.hook: Trapped in a dark boarded-up room during a multi-day blackout? Light up an entire dark room to 55W brightness using a single 1.5L water bottle—zero electricity or fire!
shortsScript.body: Burning candles during the day wastes night fuel and risks indoor fires. First, peel all labels off a crystal-clear 1.5L water bottle and lightly scuff just the upper-third grip band with sandpaper or stone. Second, fill it to the brim with clean water plus 3 drops of bleach or half a spoon of salt so green algae never grows, and seal the cap tight. Third, cut a snug hole in a cardboard or plywood window cover and insert the bottle 1/3 outside and 2/3 inside. Fourth, seal the seam watertight with pine resin or waterproof backing—instantly flooding your dark shelter with safe 55W daylight!
